chunks: Those who had stayed behind will say: 'When you depart for taking the spoils, allow us to follow you.' They wish to change the word of God. Tell them: 'You will not follow us. That is what God has already said before.' They will say: 'You are envious of our gain.' The fact is they understand but little.

key_terms.الْمُخَلَّفُونَ: The stayers behind (those who remained in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'stayers behind' in Surah Al-Fath and what did they request?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the expedition of Tabuk, where the 'stayers behind'—including prominent figures like Abdullah ibn Ubayy—feigned piety to secure a share of the spoils without enduring hardship. Their claim that they were merely following the Prophet's command is viewed as an attempt to substitute divine decree with human convenience, exposing their lack of true *fiqh* (deep understanding) of the spiritual merits of jihad. This highlights the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between outward conformity and inward sincerity in acts of worship.
